newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hit record, but run out of steam.
newsitem.headline: German shares hit record, but run out of steam.

text.p: A strongly bullish tone on the German stock market on Wednesday sent the blue chip DAX index to fresh all-time highs, but the rally lost momentum after the DAX failed to reach the magic 3,000 point level.

The DAX ended floor trade off its highs up 39.57 points, or 1.3 percent, at a record close of 2,988.45, but the IBIS DAX slid in the post-bourse session to end late electronic dealings at 2,976.56 points, 2.28 points down from Tuesday's late trading close and 20 points off the day's high.

Dealers attributed the late slide to disappointment that the DAX failed to reach 3,000 despite coming within three points of the key psychological threshold, but said the near-term outlook for the market was still good.
"I would put this down to profit-taking," said a Munich trader. "The market may have got a little overheated since Monday. But that does not mean we won't see 3,000 at all."
Wednesday's rally mainly extended gains begun in post-bourse trade on Tuesday after a benign U.S. consumer price report eased fears about a U.S. rate hike. The firm dollar underpinned the gains.
Chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks were the stars of the day.

Schering AG rose 1.60 marks to 138.90 marks in bourse trade and ended the day at 139 after its chief financial officer Klaus Pohle told a German newspaper he expected the company to keep increasing its dividends in coming years so long as profits kept rising.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG ended the day up 53 pfennigs at 21.75 marks, repairing some of its losses from Tuesday over a new draft law that would eventually limit foreign ownership of its stock. Analysts said that drop was exaggerated.
There was some concern about how long this rally would last.

Commerzbank equity strategist Thomas Tilse told Reuters Financial Television: "This looks like the best of all worlds for German stocks and we will be testing the 3,000 level. But beyond that the outlook is quite bleak."
By the end of 1997, Tilse predicted the DAX would have dropped to 2,800 points.
"Company earnings for 1997 are already priced into the market and I think realism will prevail for most of 1997."
